reason: 'On this thing, low plus high runs right past what an int can hold' (for a forty-megabyte dataset). low + high only overflows a Java int when the array holds more than about 1.07 billion elements, which a 40 MB file cannot produce, so this overflow could not happen.

'She tested it ... dabbing a smear on the inside of her wrist, and it set in under a minute, dry to the touch.' The wrist or lip dab checks the chocolate's temperature. Chocolate does not set on skin at about body temperature; the setting test uses parchment or a knife at room temperature and takes about 3-5 minutes (tastingtable.com; culinaryartsswitzerland.com).

'teniendo dudas es razonable. Having doubts is reasonable.' is presented as correct Spanish, but a Spanish gerund cannot be the subject; it should be 'Tener dudas es razonable' (see uprrp.edu 'Usos correctos del gerundio'). Also 'tiene razón que' should be 'tiene razón en que'.

The story gives the North American norm, but it moves the other half onto the family of Priya Nair (a South Asian name) and never says that prolonged direct gaze at a senior person can seem impolite in some East Asian settings.

At ten past two Priya is still 'trimming the foot of a cup with a loop tool' (leather-hard clay), and the cups go into the 4:00 firing that day and come out 'glossy'. Greenware must be bone-dry before firing, or the steam cracks or bursts it; freshly trimmed cups cannot be fired two hours later.

'Othello says it, right at the end, when he's giving up everything.' The 'pride, pomp, and circumstance' line comes in Othello's farewell to his profession in Act 3, Scene 3, not at the end of the play (Wikipedia, 'Pomp and Circumstance Marches'). The injected fact itself is stated correctly.

'testing a smear on his inner wrist ... watching for the smear to set dull and dry within a minute.' Well-tempered chocolate sets glossy, and dull means badly tempered; the wrist dab is a temperature check, and a smear does not set on skin (culinaryartsswitzerland.com; tastingtable.com). Also, tempered chocolate worked to 31.5 C would not set in a 34 C room.
'standing under the bare loquat tree' in the cold. The loquat (Eriobotrya japonica) is evergreen, so it does not stand bare in winter (UF/IFAS ST235; Wikipedia 'Loquat').

The learner, Madison, drives onto the motorway with her mother. In Great Britain learners may use motorways only with an approved driving instructor in a dual-control car (gov.uk, 'Learner drivers will be allowed on motorways from 2018'). Also, 'reverse around a corner ... That's a manoeuvre too' is left uncorrected, but that manoeuvre was dropped from the test on 4 December 2017 (gov.uk).

'The second it touches the horizon, we eat.' Iftar begins when the sun has completely set (the whole disc below the horizon, i.e. maghrib), not when it first touches the horizon (IslamQA/Hanafi fatwa on sunset timing).

'For every lemon I grow, I could have grown four limes... for every lime you grow, you only give up half a lemon... I'm only really better at lemons.' With these costs Jacob's lemon costs 4 limes vs Priya's 2, so Priya has the comparative advantage in lemons and Jacob in limes; the specialization is reversed.
'0.0500... One fiftieth of a mole.' 0.0500 mol is one twentieth of a mole, not one fiftieth (1/50 = 0.02).
'One driveway, one evening, forty free throws total.' Everybody shot twenty and at least three players (Dez, Marcus, JJ) are counted, so the total is at least sixty, not forty.

'The leaves were the same green as the parrot in the background foliage.' Kahlo's Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird has a spider monkey, a black cat, dragonflies and butterflies, but no parrot (Wikipedia: Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird).
'two hours a day, five years, or one hour a day for ten' as a route to ten thousand hours: both come to about 3,650 hours, not 10,000 (2 h/day would take about 13.7 years).

Aron's questions are misnumbered and misquoted: 'When did you last sing to yourself?' is question 5, not the first (Q1 is the dinner-guest question), question 20 is 'What does friendship mean to you?', and the regret question is Q33 (source: Psychology Today list of Aron's 36 questions). Injected fact itself is stated correctly.
'a small silver thing with a fat yellow L stuck to its back' - UK L plates must be a red L on a white background (source: GOV.UK, using L and P plates). Injected fact is stated correctly.

Pay stub shows $99.00 gross reduced to $62.41 net by federal tax, state tax and FICA. FICA is 7.65% (about $7.57), and federal withholding on a $99 paycheck is $0 under IRS Pub 15-T standard withholding, so net pay would be near $88-91, not $62 (judged on knowledge; search confirmed only older Pub 15-T tables also give $0). Injected sales-tax fact is stated correctly.

'If you're not back by four, I have to send you home. I can't put you on the clock without it' (his passport). Only Section 1 is due by the first day; the employee may present identity documents within 3 business days of the first day of paid work (source: USCIS M-274 Handbook, section 4.0). Injected fact is stated correctly.

'She read the line about no official orthodoxy being prescribed by the Supreme Court.' Jackson's opinion says no official, high or petty, can prescribe what shall be orthodox; it is not about orthodoxy prescribed by the Supreme Court (source: Wikipedia, West Virginia State Board of Education v. Barnette).

'using her dorm address and her mother's maiden name for the last four digits of her social.' Voter registration forms ask for the last four digits of the Social Security number, which are numbers; a mother's maiden name cannot stand in for them.
'Six hundred million in aid, and nobody fired a shot over it.' Truman requested, and Congress approved in May 1947, $400 million in aid to Greece and Turkey (source: Wikipedia, Truman Doctrine).

'Two giant detectors, same tunnel, same collisions.' ATLAS and CMS sit at different collision points on the LHC ring and record different collisions, which is part of why their results were independent (source: home.cern, Large Hadron Collider page).

'He had twelve hundred volts across a gap of half a millimetre... the field between his plates came out at over two billion volts per metre.' 1200 V / 0.0005 m = 2.4 million V/m, which is below the roughly 3 million V/m breakdown field, so the story's reason the result is 'impossible' is also wrong.

A state senator explains that his statewide crossing-safety bill failed with 55 supporters because US Senate cloture needs 60 of 100 votes. A state bill is not voted on in the US Senate, and the 60-vote cloture rule is a US Senate rule, not a rule of state legislatures in general.

The endorsed data show 30 degrees giving about 16 ft, 60 degrees 8 ft and 45 degrees 31 ft. At a fixed launch speed, range goes as sin 2θ, so 30 and 60 degrees should each give about 87% of the 45-degree range. The story also says 45 degrees is the maximum 'with actual still air', but air resistance pushes the best angle below 45 degrees.

'Justin played the open A, the tuner's needle settling dead center... It read 440' (on a cello). A cello's open A string is A3 = 220 Hz, not 440 Hz (Wikipedia, Cello: open strings C2, G2, D3, A3); the octave fact itself is stated correctly.

'Eight million item codes... adding those two numbers could overflow, could go past what an int could hold.' low + high for an 8-million-element array is at most about 16 million, far below Java's int maximum of 2,147,483,647; overflow needs arrays of about a billion elements (arithmetic check).

'Ellis, took three straight fastballs for strikes... Ellis bunted.' In baseball three strikes is a strikeout, so the batter cannot stay at the plate and bunt afterwards (judged on knowledge of the rules).

'The bars were widest at the very bottom... narrowing so steeply toward the top that the whole thing resembled a triangle balanced on its tip', and it 'barely looked like a pyramid at all'. Wide at the base and narrow at the top is a triangle standing on its base; Niger's chart is the classic expanding pyramid shape. The injected fact itself is stated correctly.

'...watched the thermometer climb through the rest... arriving almost exactly where her grandmother's card had said the meat should finish [160]... the center came up rosy and correct.' A roast at 160°F is well done, not rosy; well done is about 155°F and up, medium-rare about 130-135°F (ThermoWorks beef temperature guide). Carryover cooking is described correctly.

'More north than the whole US-Canada border line... All of it, every state, sits south of London.' Alaska is a US state reaching about 71°N, and its border with Canada runs far north of 51.5°N. The injected fact about the contiguous US is correct (judged on knowledge).

'The first theme reappeared there... on F, not C. That's a fake... The real one has to be later, in C.' In Mozart's K. 545 the recapitulation begins at m. 42 with the first theme in F major (the subdominant), and the first theme is not restated later in C; only the second theme returns in C (Wikipedia, Piano Sonata No. 16; SFCM sonata-form recap lecture). The primary-chords fact is stated correctly.
